key_insight: Compressibility approximations alter predicted atmospheric gravity wave displacements, wavelengths, and angles, particularly at low Froude numbers.
engineering_relevance: Capturing compressibility may improve wind farm flow and power predictions in strongly stratified atmospheric conditions.
method: Model stratified flow over bell-shaped hills.
Compare linearized Boussinesq, full incompressible Boussinesq, and fully compressible equations.
Evaluate wave displacement, apparent wavelength, and propagation angle.
evidence_signal: Simulations produce qualitatively similar wave structures, but the compressible formulation predicts larger high-altitude parcel displacements and greater apparent wavelength variation, with wave-angle differences particularly evident at low Froude numbers.
watch_item: The abstract reports idealized hill-flow simulations, not direct wind farm validation or quantified power impacts.
paper_title: Impact of compressiblity approximations on atmospheric gravity wave characteristics
